deep.reconstruction:
Context: the previous page has index tables (powers of a primitive root, and indices of the small Gaussian primes) for prime moduli of norm 37, 29, 17, 13, 9 and 5. The next page does reduction and continued-fraction style work with 9+14i. The folio therefore belongs to Gauss's work on Gaussian integers and biquadratic residues.

(A) Diagram labelled 13+8i.
- Measured on the dot lattice, the large tilted square has sides 13-8i (left vertex to bottom vertex) and 8+13i = i(13-8i) (bottom vertex to right vertex). Its circled vertices are lattice points.
- So it is the square spanned by m and i·m, with m = 13 ± 8i (orientation depends on the y-axis convention). Its area is N(m) = 169+64 = 233, which is prime.
- This square is the geometric picture of a complete residue system modulo m: one representative for each of the 233 classes.
- The small square has the same bottom vertex (call it 0). Its sides are m/2 and i·m/2, and its opposite vertex (1+i)m/2 is the centre of the large square. It is therefore one quarter of the residue square.
- Its two diagonals divide it into four triangles, labelled 0 (bottom), 1 (right), 2 (top right) and 3 (top left).
- My interpretation, not certain: this is the 'quarter system' of (233-1)/4 = 58 residues used in a Gauss-lemma-type rule for the biquadratic character. The labels 0–3 would be the exponents of the unit i^k attached to each region. Nothing on the page is computed from the figure.

(B) Lists headed 481 and 'Div. per 9+20i'.
- 481 = 13·37 = N(9+20i).
- Factorisation: 9+20i = (3-2i)(-1+6i) = (3-2i)·i·(6+i). Its conjugate is 9-20i = (3+2i)·(-i)·(6-i).
- The region in question is the quarter square 0 < x, y < 481/2 of residues mod 481.

First column. Every entry equals 13(6+i)·α = (78+13i)·α with α in the 3×3 block a+bi, a ∈ {1,2,3}, b ∈ {0,1,2}:
- α = 1+2i, 1+i, 1 give 52+169i, 65+91i, 78+13i.
- α = 2+2i, 2+i, 2 give 130+182i, 143+104i, 156+26i.
- α = 3+2i, 3+i, 3 give 208+195i, 221+117i, 234+39i.
- Within each row, x increases by 13 and y decreases by 78 (adding -i(78+13i)). Moving between rows adds 78+13i.
- I checked that these are exactly the 9 multiples of 78+13i in the quarter square. Neighbours such as α = 1+3i (39+247i), 4 (312+52i) and 2+3i (117+260i) fall outside.
- 78+13i = (9+20i)(2-3i) = (9+20i)·(-i)(3+2i). So these are the multiples of 9+20i in the quarter square that are also divisible by 3+2i, a factor of the conjugate 9-20i.

Second column: 74+111i, 148+222i, 185+37i.
- These are 37(3-2i)·β for β = i, 2i, 1+i, i.e. 37(2+3i), 37(4+6i), 37(5+i).
- They are exactly the 3 multiples of 37(3-2i) = (9+20i)(6-i) in the quarter square.
- Divided by 9+20i they give 6-i, 12-2i, 5-7i.

Taken together (my inference), the 12 entries are the multiples of 9+20i in the first-quadrant quarter system mod 481 that are not coprime to 9-20i. These are the elements one must exclude or treat separately when a lemma-type count is applied with the composite modulus 481. The small figures '2' and '4' at the right are unexplained. The scribble is illegible.
errors: No arithmetic errors found: all 12 listed numbers are correct multiples as described, and the 3×3 and 3-element lists are complete for the quarter square (0,240]×(0,240].
The page only states results; the purpose of the lists and of the triangle labelling 0–3 is not written out, so the interpretation is inferential.

results.what: Geometric representation of a complete residue system modulo the Gaussian prime 13+8i (norm 233) as a lattice square of area N(m); a quarter-square subdivided into four triangles labelled 0–3.
results.modern_name: Fundamental domain of the ideal (m) in Z[i]; quarter system for a Gauss-lemma analogue for the quartic residue symbol
results.usually_credited_to: Gauss (Theoria residuorum biquadraticorum II, 1832, geometric representation of Gaussian integers); lattice-point proofs of quartic reciprocity are associated with Eisenstein (1844)

results.what: Enumeration of the multiples of 13(6+i) and of 37(3-2i), i.e. multiples of 9+20i sharing a factor with 9-20i, lying in the quarter square of residues mod 481 = N(9+20i).
results.modern_name: Lattice points of a sublattice (ideal) in a box; residues mod a rational integer divisible by a Gaussian factor

deep.surprise_reason: Gauss's lattice picture of Gaussian residues and his quarter-system approach to biquadratic residues are known from TRB II and the Werke Nachlass. This page is a worked numerical illustration (modulus 13+8i, composite 481) with no new theorem visible.

checkable.asserts: 13+8i has prime norm 233, so the diagram square has 233 residue classes
the first column consists of the multiples (78+13i)*alpha
exactly 9 multiples of 78+13i lie in the quarter square, so the first list is complete
the second column entries are divisible by 9+20i
exactly 3 multiples of 37(3-2i)=111-74i lie in the quarter square, so the second list is complete
78+13i = (9+20i)(2-3i), so the first list consists of multiples of 9+20i
